title: Standard versus Express workflows (durability and cost)
hook: Step Functions Standard workflows persist every state transition for up to a year — ideal for auditable business processes. Express workflows trade full history for speed and lower cost on high-volume runs under five minutes.

blocks.text: Standard workflows: durable execution history, exactly-once state transition semantics, up to one year duration, higher per-transition cost. Express workflows: at-least-once execution, max five minutes, high throughput, logs to CloudWatch Logs instead of full console history. Pick based on audit requirements and volume.

entries.plainDefinition: Durable workflow with full execution history in console.
entries.example: Order saga with human approval wait.

entries.plainDefinition: High-throughput workflow under 5 minutes with reduced history.
entries.example: IoT telemetry aggregation per device batch.

blocks.text: Payment orchestration on Express loses granular console audit — compliance may reject. Million-events-per-day on Standard bleeds cost. Express synchronous invoke from API Gateway suits sub-second orchestration; Standard suits multi-day workflows with waitForTaskToken.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: Standard for sagas, compliance, long waits. Express for volume, short duration, lower cost. Cannot convert type in place — new state machine.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Volume and cost
items.body: Millions/day short flows → Express with CloudWatch Logs.

diagram.title: Standard vs Express decision

snippet.label: CloudFormation — Standard state machine
snippet.code:
Resources:
  OrderStateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: order-saga
      StateMachineType: STANDARD
      RoleArn: !GetAtt SfnRole.Arn
      LoggingConfiguration:
        Level: ERROR
        Destinations:
          - CloudWatchLogsLogGroup:
              LogGroupArn: !GetAtt SfnLogGroup.Arn
      DefinitionString: !Sub |
        { "StartAt": "Validate", "States": { "Validate": { "Type": "Pass", "End": true } } }
snippet.explanation: StateMachineType STANDARD explicit. Logging still recommended for prod debug.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — Express with full log level
snippet.code:
TelemetryStateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineName: telemetry-aggregate
      StateMachineType: EXPRESS
      LoggingConfiguration:
        Level: ALL
        IncludeExecutionData: true
        Destinations:
          - CloudWatchLogsLogGroup:
              LogGroupArn: !GetAtt ExpressLogGroup.Arn
snippet.explanation: Express relies on CloudWatch Logs for detail — IncludeExecutionData for input/output in logs.

snippet.label: CLI — compare execution metrics
snippet.code:
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics \
  --namespace AWS/States \
  --metric-name ExecutionsStarted \
  --dimensions Name=StateMachineArn,Value=arn:aws:states:us-east-1:123:stateMachine:orders \
  --start-time 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2026-01-02T00:00:00Z \
  --period 3600 --statistics Sum
snippet.explanation: Volume metric drives Express vs Standard cost model decision.

snippet.label: CLI — synchronous Express invoke from API
snippet.explanation: Sync Express returns result inline — suitable for API Gateway Lambda proxy replacement.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Express for payment saga needing audit. Standard for 10M daily 200ms flows — cost explosion. No logging on Express — blind in prod. Assuming you can change type on existing state machine.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: cost explorer Step Functions line item; divide ExecutionsStarted by bill. Standard ExecutionsFailed visible in console; Express query Logs Insights on log group. Provisioned throughput mode on Express for guaranteed capacity.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'Express is just cheaper Standard.' Strong answer: different durability, history, duration limits, and at-least-once semantics on Express.

interviewTakeaways: Standard: durable, full history, up to 1 year — sagas and compliance.
Express: high volume, <5 min, logs to CloudWatch — lower cost per run.
Cannot change workflow type in place — create new state machine and migrate.
60s: Standard audit and long waits. Express volume short jobs. Five min cap Express. Logs not console history.
Follow-up: Express at-least-once — how does that affect Task design?
commonPitfalls: Express for regulated payment audit — rejection answer.
Strong answer: Standard with logging and retention for compliance workflows.
Standard for million daily short executions — cost and scale mismatch.
No CloudWatch Logs on Express — cannot debug production failures.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Standard Step Functions resembles Temporal workflow durability — Express is closer to a single Lambda chain without persisted event history.
Bull completed job log is like Standard history; Express is like fire-and-forget with only application logs.
